semantics: interleaving; exhaustive up to the state cap

results.name: Authentication Integrity
results.description: No device may reach Malware Execution without having passed through the Authenticate transition. The transition is a cut vertex on every path into the hazardous place.

results.name: Safe State Reachability
results.formula: AG EF (∀d . place(d) ∈ {Idle, Normal, Isolation, Recovery})
results.description: From every reachable state the system retains a path back to a marking in which every device is safe. No compromise is terminal.

results.name: Deadlock Freedom
results.description: The net contains no dead marking: from every reachable state at least one transition remains enabled.

results.name: Isolation Successful
results.description: Once a device is quarantined, no transmitting transition is enabled for it — neither exfiltration nor lateral infection as a source.

results.name: Malware Containment
results.description: Every device that reaches Malware Execution must inevitably reach Isolation. Reachability is not enough — the eventuality has to hold on every path.
counterexample: <antecedent holds here — the eventuality must now follow>

results.name: Data Leakage Prevention
results.description: No execution contains a state in which data leaves a device before the detector has ruled on it. Checked as an invariant, which is sound for a safety formula over a finite structure.

results.name: Critical Asset Safety
results.description: The industrial controller never reaches a confirmed-threat state. This is a class-specific guarantee: it quantifies over the device class carried in the token colour, which a flat state-only colour set could not express.

results.name: Lateral Movement Bound
results.description: At most two devices are ever simultaneously in a confirmed-threat state. Bounds the blast radius of lateral propagation across the modelled segment.

scenarios.title: Compromised gateway → vulnerable actuator (same zone)
scenarios.rationale: The gateway holds the management plane and shared credentials, so its route to an actuator is strong (2). The thermostat is only standard-hardened (1). 2 > 1, so propagation is admitted.

scenarios.title: Compromised gateway → hardened industrial controller
scenarios.rationale: The same compromised gateway, and the plant zone is routable from the building zone. But the gateway→PLC route is weak (1) and the controller is fully hardened (2). 1 > 2 is false, so the guard denies propagation. Reachability alone is not sufficient — the pair relation decides.

guard.explanation: route strength 1 does not overcome hardening 2

scenarios.title: Compromised sensor → temperature actuator
scenarios.rationale: The interaction raised in supervision. An actuator that consumes a sensor topic without validating the payload gives the sensor a strong route (2) against standard hardening (1). Propagation is admitted — and note the sensor could not reach a camera at all.

scenarios.title: Compromised sensor → smart camera
scenarios.rationale: Same compromised sensor, same zone, same hardening as the actuator above — but no route exists between these classes (strength 0). The difference in outcome is attributable to device class alone, which is precisely what a state-only colour set could not express.

guard.explanation: no route exists from Motion Sensor to Smart Camera

scenarios.title: Cross-zone: compromised clinical monitor → plant controller
scenarios.rationale: Segmentation, not susceptibility. The clinical and plant zones are mutually unreachable under the segment policy, so the guard fails on the zone conjunct before susceptibility is ever considered.

guard.explanation: zone clinical cannot route to plant

scenarios.title: Cross-zone permitted: compromised gateway → clinical monitor
scenarios.rationale: The building zone adjoins the clinical VLAN, and an unpatched monitor (0) falls to the gateway route (1). Shows the zone relation permitting as well as denying — the control is a policy, not a blanket block.
